subject: A Level Biology
title: Fluid mosaic model
question:
Fig. 8.1 shows part of a cell surface membrane.
(a) Identify the structures labelled A to E.
(b) Explain why the membrane is described as fluid mosaic.
(c) Suggest why ions cross the membrane through C and not between the phospholipids.

scene: The renderer cannot repeat shapes, so Claude listed all 64 phospholipids one by one. It works, but the description is long.
tikz: TikZ can repeat shapes in a loop, so the bilayer takes only a few lines.
svg: First try: label A was placed above the top edge of the image and got cut off.
Second try: made the image taller.

figure:
Part of a cell surface membrane in the fluid mosaic model, side view.
A phospholipid bilayer: two rows of round heads facing outwards, each with two tails pointing into the middle.
One large protein spans the whole bilayer. It has a carbohydrate chain, a short chain of small circles, attached on top, making a glycoprotein.
A channel protein made of two parts spans the bilayer with a gap between them.
A small cholesterol molecule sits among the tails in one layer.
Use label lines with letters only: A to the carbohydrate chain, B to a phospholipid head, C to the channel through the channel protein, D to the cholesterol and E to the tails.
Caption: Fig. 8.1.
